title: Restaurant health inspection posters and what they mean

paragraphs: Food facilities must post the red, green, or yellow "placard" related to their last health inspection.

sections.heading: What the signs mean
paragraphs: To check the food safety at San Francisco restaurants, look for green, yellow, or red placards. The restaurant must post the placard where the public can see it.

sections.heading: What the signs mean › Green : Pass
paragraphs: The facility had zero to 1 major violations observed at time of inspection. If the restaurant had a major violation, it was corrected at the time of the inspection.

sections.heading: What the signs mean › Yellow : Conditional pass
paragraphs: The facility had 2 or more major violations observed at the time of the routine inspection. At the time of the inspection, the restaurant corrected the major violations.
We will conduct a re-inspection and issue a new placard based on the results.

sections.heading: What the signs mean › Red : Closed
paragraphs: We closed the facility because there are health hazards or major violations that can't be fixed right away.
The unsafe conditions must be corrected before the facility can reopen.
